newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany to check up on "sick" civil servants.
newsitem.headline: Germany to check up on "sick" civil servants.

text.p: The German cabinet agreed on Tuesday that government employees who call in sick from work should receive home visits to check whether they really are ill.
Trade unions criticised the move as "undignified snooping" into workers' private lives.
Interior Minister Manfred Kanther said that on average government employees missed 17 days a year, three days more than comparable workers in the private sector.
To improve job attendance, he planned to draft a list of measures that include home visits to employees who call in sick and requiring a doctor's note from the first day of illness.
At present employees who call in sick need a doctor's note only after their third day off.
The government's scare tactics are meant to rein in rising costs and make public administration more efficient.
